title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(増田達男研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Masuta Tatsuo)
keywords: Urban Habitation 2.Housing Environment 3.Historical District 4.Fieldwork and Regional Collaboration 5.Data Analysis
educationalGoal: Study field is habitation in urban area. The research theme presupposes social significance and the conditions under which the research is established. Necessary data is collected through fieldwork and map surveys rooted in the region in accordance with the research theme. Analyze the data to clarify logically and systematically what has been unknown so far and what to evaluate. Eventually, findings that will help solve the problem will be compiled into a research paper.
advice: 1) Review and final decision of project proposal Appropriate themes will be determined in light of the research targets, while focusing on the target area of interest. 2) Promotion of project First semester: ① Prior to research, the same task is initially performed jointly. It is to recognize the scope of the field and the research method. ② Necessary data is collected through fieldwork and map surveys in accordance with the research theme. Second semester: The results obtained by analyzing the data need to be logically organized. And compose them in a research paper. 3) Advice Take care of yourself day by day, move forward and think repeatedly. You will get great results over time.
books: Textbook: Not specified Reference book: Not specified Reserved block: Not specified
requiredKnowledge: A well-balanced knowledge of the architectural field will help you. Get interested in this field and experience the real urban area as much as possible.

activityGoals.body: You can recognize about the habitation district in the real urban area.
You can collect research data through fieldwork or surveys on maps.
You can set up the necessary system for analysis based on the obtained research data.
You can organize and logically analyze your research data according to the theme.
You can systematically organize the results of your analysis and put them together in a research paper.
